Choosing a cleaning rule

Source: vignettes/rules.Rmd
rules.Rmd

flag_occurrences() writes one flag per record and test and removes nothing. A cleaning rule is a set of tests: a record is dropped when it carries any of them. This article flags a set of records once, measures what share each test and each candidate rule would remove, overall and by group, and then applies the chosen rule. All of the comparisons below reuse the flags from that single pass.

  1. Flag the records once with every test of interest, flag_occurrences().

  2. Measure the share each test and rule removes, summary() and plot().

  3. Break it down by taxon, record age and coordinate precision, tally_flags() with by and bins.

  4. Apply the chosen rule, has_flag().

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner")

Needs a C++ compiler (Rtools on Windows).

Example 

library(OccurrenceCleaner)

Records with known errors

The example records are random points on land in Europe, drawn by rejecting points the sea test flags, with species, kingdom, year and the GBIF fields a download carries. Older records get larger coordinate uncertainty and are more often rounded, as in real GBIF data.

set.seed(42)
n <- 3000
lon <- runif(3 * n, -10, 30)
lat <- runif(3 * n, 36, 60)
sea <- flag_occurrences(data.frame(decimalLongitude = lon, decimalLatitude = lat),
                        tests = "sea")$flag_sea
x <- data.frame(decimalLongitude = round(lon[!sea][1:n], 4),
                decimalLatitude = round(lat[!sea][1:n], 4),
                kingdom = sample(c("Animalia", "Plantae", "Fungi"), n, TRUE, c(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)),
                species = paste("species", sample(60, n, TRUE)),
                year = sample(1850:2024, n, TRUE, prob = exp(seq(-3, 0, length.out = 175))))
old <- x$year < 1970
x$coordinateUncertaintyInMeters <- round(rlnorm(n, ifelse(old, 8, 4), 1))
x$coordinateUncertaintyInMeters[sample(n, 600)] <- NA
x$basisOfRecord <- ifelse(old, "PRESERVED_SPECIMEN", "HUMAN_OBSERVATION")
x$basisOfRecord[sample(n, 15)] <- "FOSSIL_SPECIMEN"
x$issue <- ifelse(runif(n) < ifelse(old, 0.3, 0.03), "COORDINATE_ROUNDED", "")
x$issue[sample(n, 40)] <- "TAXON_MATCH_FUZZY;GEODETIC_DATUM_ASSUMED_WGS84"

Then the errors are planted: records placed within 3 km of five capitals, records at (0, 0), records in the Atlantic and exact copies of earlier records.

capitals <- data.frame(lon = c(16.37, 2.35, 13.40, -3.70, 12.50),
                       lat = c(48.21, 48.86, 52.52, 40.42, 41.90))
i <- sample(n, 150); j <- sample(5, 150, TRUE)
x$decimalLongitude[i] <- capitals$lon[j] + runif(150, -0.02, 0.02)
x$decimalLatitude[i] <- capitals$lat[j] + runif(150, -0.02, 0.02)
i <- sample(setdiff(seq_len(n), i), 40)
x[i, c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude")] <- 0
i <- sample(n, 60)
x$decimalLongitude[i] <- runif(60, -25, -15)
x$decimalLatitude[i] <- runif(60, 40, 55)
x <- rbind(x, x[sample(n, 120), ])
nrow(x)
#> [1] 3120

Flag once

The tests are the defaults (the CoordinateCleaner-equivalent tests that need only coordinates and a species), the GBIF issue flags on coordinates and rounding, and the fossil test on the basis of record.

tests <- c(default_tests(), "issue_coordinate", "issue_rounded", "basis_fossil")
f <- flag_occurrences(x, tests = tests)
class(f)
#> [1] "occ_flags"  "data.frame"

The result is x with a flags column and one logical flag_<test> column per test. Its class, occ_flags, is what summary() and plot() dispatch on.

What each test removes

summary() turns the flags into shares of records. Without a rules argument it uses one rule, all, holding every test that was run.

summary(f)
#> <occ_summary> 3,120 records
#>   rule all: removes 749 (24.01 %)
#>  rule              test    n flagged   pct only pct_only
#>   all           invalid 3120       0  0.00    0     0.00
#>   all              zero 3120      40  1.28    0     0.00
#>   all             equal 3120      40  1.28    0     0.00
#>   all           capital 3120     160  5.13  124     3.97
#>   all          centroid 3120      16  0.51    1     0.03
#>   all       institution 3120      40  1.28    0     0.00
#>   all gbif_headquarters 3120       0  0.00    0     0.00
#>   all               sea 3120     105  3.37   52     1.67
#>   all         duplicate 3120     130  4.17   92     2.95
#>   all  issue_coordinate 3120       0  0.00    0     0.00
#>   all     issue_rounded 3120     411 13.17  361    11.57
#>   all      basis_fossil 3120      15  0.48   12     0.38
#>   all             (any) 3120     749 24.01

For each test of the rule, flagged is the number of records carrying that test and pct the same as a percentage of all records. only counts the records for which that test is the sole flag among the rule’s tests: dropping that test from the rule would keep exactly these records. The row (any) is the rule itself, the records that carry at least one of its tests.

A record can fail several tests at once. The 40 records at (0, 0) are flagged by zero, equal (|0| = |0|), sea and institution, so none of them is counted under only. The per-test shares therefore add up to more than the rule’s total, while the only shares add up to at most that total; the difference is the records removed for more than one reason. Both figures are needed to say why records are lost: pct is how often a problem occurs, pct_only is how much of the loss would disappear without that test.

The same numbers as a plot: the full bar is pct, the dark part pct_only.

plot(f)

Comparing rules

Candidate rules go into rules as a named list. Here strict uses all the tests, cc the CoordinateCleaner tests without the duplicate test, and minimal only the tests for coordinates that cannot be right.

rules <- list(strict = tests,
              cc = setdiff(default_tests(), "duplicate"),
              minimal = c("invalid", "zero", "sea"))
s <- summary(f, rules = rules)
s[s$test == "(any)", c("rule", "n", "flagged", "pct")]
#>     rule    n flagged   pct
#>   strict 3120     749 24.01
#>       cc 3120     266  8.53
#>  minimal 3120     105  3.37

The summary is a data frame of class occ_summary, so rows can be selected as usual; the selection above keeps one row per rule. plot() draws one rule at a time:

plot(s, rule = "cc")

In this example every record the institution test flags is also flagged by zero: GBIF’s registry of scientific collections holds an entry geocoded about 11 m from (0, 0), so each zero-coordinate record also lies within 100 m of an institution. The capital test, by contrast, is the sole reason for most of its records.

By group

The arguments of tally_flags() pass through summary(), so by splits the shares by any column of the records.

s <- summary(f, rules = rules["cc"], by = "kingdom")
s[s$test %in% c("capital", "sea", "(any)"), ]
#> <occ_summary> 3,120 records, grouped by kingdom
#>   kingdom rule    test    n flagged  pct only pct_only
#>  Animalia   cc capital 1546      85 5.50   80     5.17
#>  Animalia   cc     sea 1546      53 3.43   33     2.13
#>  Animalia   cc   (any) 1546     138 8.93              
#>     Fungi   cc capital  312      15 4.81   12     3.85
#>     Fungi   cc     sea  312      10 3.21    6     1.92
#>     Fungi   cc   (any)  312      25 8.01              
#>   Plantae   cc capital 1262      60 4.75   53     4.20
#>   Plantae   cc     sea 1262      42 3.33   26     2.06
#>   Plantae   cc   (any) 1262     103 8.16

With grouping, plot() shows a grid of tests by groups, shaded by the share each test flags in each group, with the rule itself in the bottom row.

plot(f, rules = rules["cc"], by = "kingdom")

Record age and coordinate precision

Year and coordinate uncertainty stay raw columns of the records and are cut into classes only when tallying. bins takes the break points and adds a <column>_bin grouping column, with missing values in their own class.

t <- tally_flags(f, rules = rules,
                 bins = list(year = c(1900, 1950, 1970, 2000)))
s <- summary(t)
s[s$rule == "strict" & s$test %in% c("issue_rounded", "(any)"),
  c("year_bin", "test", "n", "pct")]
#>   year_bin          test    n   pct
#>      <1900 issue_rounded  240 30.00
#>      <1900         (any)  240 40.42
#>  1900-1950 issue_rounded  526 30.99
#>  1900-1950         (any)  526 38.02
#>  1950-1970 issue_rounded  362 30.39
#>  1950-1970         (any)  362 37.29
#>  1970-2000 issue_rounded  852  3.52
#>  1970-2000         (any)  852 14.67
#>     >=2000 issue_rounded 1140  3.16
#>     >=2000         (any) 1140 16.84

tally_flags() returns the counts; summary() on its result gives the percentages, and plot() the grid. The tally is the one to keep when the counts will be summed or merged later.

plot(t, rule = "strict")

The same works for the stated coordinate uncertainty, where the classes are distances in metres:

t <- tally_flags(f, rules = rules["strict"],
                 bins = list(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = c(100, 1000, 10000)))
s <- summary(t)
s[s$test %in% c("issue_rounded", "(any)"),
  c("coordinateUncertaintyInMeters_bin", "test", "n", "pct")]
#>  coordinateUncertaintyInMeters_bin          test    n   pct
#>                               <100 issue_rounded 1159  3.97
#>                               <100         (any) 1159 17.86
#>                           100-1000 issue_rounded  567  9.35
#>                           100-1000         (any)  567 18.87
#>                         1000-10000 issue_rounded  664 30.12
#>                         1000-10000         (any)  664 38.70
#>                            >=10000 issue_rounded  111 31.53
#>                            >=10000         (any)  111 36.94
#>                            missing issue_rounded  619 12.44
#>                            missing         (any)  619 22.13

Where the removed records are

On a flagged data frame, plot(type = "map") draws the records over the Natural Earth land, coloured by whether the first rule of rules removes them.

plot(f, type = "map", rules = rules["cc"])

Applying the rule

has_flag() returns TRUE for every record carrying at least one test of the rule, so the cleaned table is the complement.

clean <- f[!has_flag(f$flags, rules$cc), ]
nrow(clean)
#> [1] 2854

The removed records keep their flags, and a different rule only needs a different set of tests in the same call; the records never have to be flagged again. A cut on record age or uncertainty is an ordinary filter on the raw columns, for example clean[clean$year >= 1950, ].

How the shares are computed

All counts come from the integer flag word. For a rule with tests TT and the bit mask mTm_T of those tests (flag_mask(T)), a record with flag word ww is

  • flagged by test tt when bit tt of ww is set,

  • removed by the rule when w&mT≠0w \mathbin{\&} m_T \neq 0,

  • removed by tt alone when w&mT=mtw \mathbin{\&} m_T = m_t.

tally_flags() counts these per group in one pass over the flags, which is also how it runs on on-disk output part by part (see Large tables on disk). The percentages in summary() divide each count by the number of records in its group.
